newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy committee head urges car incentive extension.
newsitem.headline: Italy committee head urges car incentive extension.

text.p: The chairman of Italy's lower house parliamentary transport committee, Ernesto Stajano, on Tuesday said he was in favour of extending a nine-month national car buying incentive scheme started at the beginning of the year.

"I believe that it is possible to think of extending the car buying incentive scheme by six months," said Stajano while attending a conference here, and added that this would be an idea to achieve a "soft landing" for the car market.

Italy's new car market has been driven higher by the incentive scheme with new car registrations up 43.23 percent in May this year from May 1996, but there are signs that new car orders are now beginning to slow down.

On Monday, the managing director of carmaker Fiat Paolo Cantarella told the group's annual shareholders meeting the incentive scheme had given results ahead of expectations but similar schemes by other countries had run for longer than nine months.

Italy introduced its scheme at the start of January, which is scheduled to run to end-September, whereby owners of cars of over 10 years old can trade their vehicles in for scrapping to receive a price discount on the purchase of a new car.

Italy's vehicle makers association Anfia also on Monday called for tax breaks to encourage the car market, adding that all motor vehicle tax income -- included VAT, new registration and petrol tax -- would raise around 121 trillion lire in 1997, up eight percent from 1996, and would account for 21.6 percent of all tax income.

Earlier this month, car research body Centro Studi Promotor (CSP) said the car incentive scheme had cost the government some 574 billion lire in the first five months of 1997, but added that income from VAT and new car registration tax brought to the state 1.051 trillion lire, giving the Italian government a net benefit of 477 billion lire.
